ag/gemini-3.8-flash.observation: All four cases completed. Responses commonly used markdown JSON fences, so semantic normalization succeeded while strict protocol compliance remained false.

ag/gemini-3.8-flash-high.observation: LS-02 completed with exact schema and no fence. NS-04, XP-01 and TU-04 timed out at roughly 90 seconds.

oc/muse-spark-1.2-contributor-free.observation: All four bake-off cases failed semantic JSON normalization. A follow-up raw probe also did not complete within the probe window.

oc/muse-spark-1.3-contributor-free.observation: All four bake-off cases failed semantic JSON normalization. A follow-up raw probe also did not complete within the probe window.

findings: Semantic model quality and protocol compliance must be scored separately.
Gemini 3.8 Flash currently has the best operational completeness among tested candidates.
Gemini 3.8 Flash produced rich conflict/context classifications on the diagnostic cases, but the current gold labels are too coarse to treat contextual/contradiction decisions as pure errors.
Gemini 3.8 Flash High showed stronger strict schema compliance on the one completed case but unacceptable latency/timeouts on the other three.
Muse 1.2 and 1.3 are not benchmark-ready in the current adapter path; their failure mode is JSON/response normalization rather than a demonstrated semantic-quality failure.
decision: Do not declare a permanent semantic-assessor winner. Use ag/gemini-3.8-flash as the provisional treatment candidate for the next frozen benchmark, while improving the gold taxonomy and instrumenting Muse raw responses separately.
next_step: Expand worthiness gold taxonomy with direct_support, supporting, contextual, contradiction, obsolete/proposed labels.
Run a small fixed human/oracle audit on the same 4 cases.
Re-test Gemini 3.8 Flash on the expanded taxonomy.
Build a raw-response capture path for Muse so parse failures remain diagnosable.
Only then run the 16-case semantic treatment benchmark.
